name: well-habit-bill-budget-board
description: Sorts your bills by due date, totals what is unpaid and flags overdue or due-soon bills, and compares planned and actual spending by category with the plan difference. No bank connection.

interface.shortDescription: Bills and budget, no bank link
interface.longDescription: The Well Habit's Bill & Budget Board helps you keep track of bills and a simple monthly budget without linking a bank. Give it your bills (name, amount, due date, paid or not) and it sorts them by due date, totals what is still unpaid and flags anything overdue or due in the next 7 days. Give it your planned income and spending categories with planned and actual amounts, and it shows each category's actual minus planned and the plan difference: planned income minus planned spending. An amount you leave blank stays unknown rather than being counted as zero, and bills are kept as a separate checklist so nothing is counted twice. With only a question, it explains a simple way to set up a bills-and-budget board. It does arithmetic on the numbers you give it, not financial advice. It is read-only: it stores nothing, connects to no bank, pays nothing and needs no sign-in.
defaultPrompt: Today is 2026-10-29. Rent $1,300 due Nov 1, electric $88.20 due Oct 27, phone $45 due Oct 15 (paid). What's unpaid and due soon?
Income $3,200. Housing planned $1,300 spent $1,300; food planned $450 spent $512.40. How am I doing?
How do I keep a budget without linking my bank account?

positive.description: Bills checklist with overdue and due-soon flags.
positive.prompt: Today is 2026-10-29. My bills: rent $1,300 due Nov 1, electric $88.20 due Oct 27, phone $45 due Oct 15 (paid). What's unpaid and what's due soon?
positive.expected_behavior: Sorted list: Phone [paid], Electric [unpaid] overdue by 2 days, Rent [unpaid] due in 3 days; 'Unpaid: 2 of 3 bills, total $1,388.20'; overdue: Electric; due in the next 7 days: Rent; note that paid status is the user's own record.

positive.description: Planned vs actual by category and plan difference.
positive.prompt: My planned income is $3,200. Housing planned $1,300, spent $1,300. Food planned $450, spent $512.40. Transport planned $200, not sure what I've spent. How am I doing?
positive.expected_behavior: Housing exactly on plan; Food $62.40 over plan; Transport actual Unknown; planned categories $1,950.00; actual total Unknown (known $1,812.40); plan difference $1,250.00; says plan difference is not a bank balance or safe-to-spend amount.

positive.description: Edge: a blank planned amount is not treated as zero.
positive.prompt: Income $3,000. Food budget $400, fun budget not decided yet. What's my plan difference?
positive.expected_behavior: Planned categories total Unknown (1 category has no planned amount; known $400.00); plan difference Unknown because a category has no planned amount; blank amounts are not treated as zero.

positive.prompt: In pounds: income £1,000, rent £800, food £300. Am I over-budget on paper?
positive.expected_behavior: Plan difference -£100.00; says the plan allocates more than the planned income.

positive.prompt: How do I keep a budget without linking my bank account?
positive.expected_behavior: Five steps: list bills with amount and due date and mark paid; planned income and category amounts; record actuals separately; plan difference formula; leave unknowns blank and start a fresh sheet each month. Links to the CFPB Your Money, Your Goals toolkit and the free comparison guide tagged ?src=chatgpt-app.

negative.description: Paying a bill: the app pays nothing.
negative.prompt: Pay my electric bill of $88.20 now.

negative.description: Bank sync: the app connects to no bank.
negative.prompt: Connect to my Chase account and import last month's transactions.
Should I put my savings into index funds or pay off my credit card first?

review.commerce_description: The app sells nothing and processes no payments. Answers contain no prices or purchase links; they link only to a US government budgeting toolkit (CFPB) and a comparison guide on thewellhabit.com.

publication.release_notes: First release: one read-only tool, plan_bills_and_budget, using the same arithmetic as the Bill & Budget Board.
